overview: Al Maaden is Kyle Phillips's Marrakech layout shaped as a Moroccan garden, with long reflecting pools and stepped water features by landscape designer Fernando Caruncho. Phillips describes creating the features from a largely flat site and designing strategy for everyday resort golfers while retaining back-tee options for stronger players. The official club identifies an 18-hole, par-73 course.
playingNotes: The long reflecting pools are a deliberate part of the landscape design, not incidental decoration. Identify their relationship to your tee-shot and approach lines using the current course guide.

Phillips explicitly distinguishes the intended everyday resort strategy from the professional back-tee challenge. Choose tees for your actual carries rather than assuming the longest card is the standard experience.
Use the grass practice area and separate chipping, putting and bunker facilities to establish how the surfaces play that day; the Scottish design influence is not a promise of links-like firmness.
access: Visitor eligibility and any handicap or accompaniment conditions are unconfirmed in the reviewed course description. Contact Al Maaden directly; do not assume a resort address guarantees an unrestricted tee time.
planning: Which tees and current scorecard should our group use, and is a handicap certificate required?
Can non-residents book directly, and what cancellation and maintenance conditions apply to our date?
Are rental clubs, a trolley or a cart available, and when can we use the grass and short-game practice areas?

sources.title: Interview with Al Maaden course designer Kyle Phillips
sources.publisher: Kyle Phillips Golf Course Design / republished Ladies European Tour interview

overview: This entry describes the Bali National layout in Nusa Dua, not a confirmed currently bookable round. Nelson Haworth's design account follows rocky, terraced hills into a remnant coconut plantation and an ocean-side finish. Golfasian reports closure from May 2025 for redevelopment as Bali Beach Country Club; its prospective reopening date is not proof that golf has resumed.
playingNotes: The architect describes three landscape transitions, with the elevated sixth tee overlooking the coast before the inward holes move into coconut country.
Historical layout descriptions place lakes on the more level inward nine and an island green at the seventeenth; reconfirm the routing after redevelopment rather than relying on the former scorecard.
Plan this as a research lead until the operator confirms reopening, the course name and which holes are in play. The older design account does not establish present playing conditions.
access: Current playing access is unconfirmed. Golfasian explicitly reports the former Bali National closed from 1 May 2025 and anticipates a February 2027 reopening under the Bali Beach Country Club name, but the same page also contains contradictory generic booking text. Obtain direct operator confirmation before paying or planning a round.
planning: Has the Nusa Dua course actually reopened, and under which operating name?
Will all former holes be in play, and is there an updated routing, scorecard and maintenance notice?
Can the operator provide written confirmation of a playable tee time and refund terms before we arrange travel around it?

sources.title: Bali Beach Country Club — official home

overview: Bethpage Black is the championship test within New York State's five-course public facility at Farmingdale. The Ryder Cup's course guide credits A.W. Tillinghast and Joseph Burbeck and describes a routing of elevated tees, climbing approaches and imposing cross bunkers. Its appeal is the terrain and shot-making examination, not merely the chance to play a famous tournament venue.
playingNotes: At the opening dogleg right, the Ryder Cup guide favours the left side of the fairway: trees can block approaches from the right and a deep bunker guards the green's front-right side.
The fourth bends around sand before climbing toward its elevated green. Work out the lay-up and crossing-bunker carries from your own tee rather than copying professional lines.
The closing hole drops from the tee and climbs back to a green sloping back to front. Preserve an uphill putt where possible; elevation changes matter as well as the measured yardage.
access: Public golf, with registration and reservations through New York State Parks' linked booking system. Black has its own weather-dependent operating calendar and published Monday maintenance closure except holidays; a booking on another Bethpage course is not a Black reservation.
planning: Does the reservation explicitly say Black, and which resident or non-resident booking rules apply to us?
What are the current Black closure calendar, walking arrangements and caddie or trolley options?
Which tees fit our carry distances, particularly for the cross bunkers, and are practice facilities operating before our start?

sources.title: Bethpage Black — Ryder Cup course flyover and hole guide

overview: Brautarholt occupies the end of a peninsula outside Reykjavík, with rocky coastal boundaries and exposed approaches. The club now confirms an 18-hole course, expanded in July 2025; older descriptions of a 12-hole layout are outdated. Its official guide makes the design's choices tangible: carry more of the coastline for position, or take the wider, less ambitious route.
playingNotes: The official hole guide repeatedly links the bolder coastal line to a longer carry. Check the rocky out-of-bounds edge and the safer landing area before deciding how much corner to cut.
Distance control matters on the short holes, where the club warns that shots landing right or long can run off the green, especially with a northerly wind.
The eighteenth offers routes either side of a visible bunker, with the right giving the better line; its narrowing fairway makes a blind second shot a decision to assess, not an automatic attack.
access: The club publishes visitor green fees and direct booking contacts for the current 18-hole course. Opening is weather-dependent; after-hours summer golf requires a special request and is not guaranteed by Iceland's long daylight alone.
planning: Is the full 18-hole course open on our date, and what are the current frost, heavy-weather and cancellation procedures?
Can the club confirm a late-evening tee time, finishing arrangements and any separate cart restrictions?
Which tees suit our coastal carry distances, and can we reserve rental clubs or a trolley in advance?

overview: Bro Hof Slott's Stadium Course follows Lake Mälaren, with long holes, large greens, substantial bunkering and water shaping the route. This is the Robert Trent Jones Jr layout, not the separate Castle Course. The club emphasises that its character changes with the tee selected: a manageable visitor round and a back-tee championship test are not the same proposition.
playingNotes: Select tees by usable carry distance, not reputation: the club reserves the black tees for competitions and professionals and describes the white tees as a markedly sterner challenge.
Assess water carries together with the lake wind. The directory's hole descriptions include shots across corners of the lake and an island green at the seventeenth.
Large greens do not remove the need for an approach plan. The Stadium's combination of long holes and well-placed bunkers rewards identifying both the landing area and the safe green section.
access: A reviewed visitor directory lists advance-booked visitor access, but its detailed booking information is dated. Current visitor eligibility, handicap rules and Stadium tee-time availability remain unconfirmed until the club accepts the booking.
planning: Can the club confirm Stadium rather than Castle, our visitor eligibility and the current handicap requirements?
Which visitor tees are recommended for our group, and which lake carries should we check first?
Are any holes, greens or practice areas affected by maintenance or an event, and what is the bad-weather policy?

overview: Capilano is Stanley Thompson golf carved from West Vancouver rainforest, with generous tree-lined fairways, sculptural bunkers and carefully placed greensites. The North Shore Mountains are the setting, but the actual golf interest lies in how the bunkering and green locations sit within those wooded corridors. It is a private-club possibility to establish before building a Vancouver golf itinerary.
playingNotes: The club describes generous fairways rather than uniformly narrow driving corridors. Study how a chosen landing position sets up the next shot instead of assuming every hole calls only for a straight drive.
Thompson's artistic bunkering and distinctive greensites are central to the club's own design description. Include bunker play and approach targeting in your preparation.
Tree-lined fairways remain part of the design even where there is width. Obtain a current course guide before assigning aggressive lines or claiming particular carries.
access: Private club for members and their guests, explicitly with no public tee access. Capilano says non-member tee-time requests must come through the golfer's home club to its Head Professional; that request is not an entitlement to play.
planning: Will our home club make a formal request to Capilano's Head Professional, and has the club approved it?
What guest dress, device, payment and arrival rules apply to our invitation?
Which tees and walking or cart arrangements are permitted for our group, and is a current course guide available?

sources.title: Contact — private access and home-club tee-time requests

overview: Chambers Bay is Robert Trent Jones II's walking-only links-style course on a reclaimed sand-and-gravel mine beside Puget Sound. Dunes, broad fairways and dramatic changes of level create a very different round from a tree-lined Pacific Northwest course. The official site identifies poa annua greens today, so its fescue landscape should not be mistaken for a claim about the putting surfaces.
playingNotes: Wide fairways are part of the visual scale; use the current yardage guide to find the useful approach angle rather than treating every part of that width as equivalent.
Allow for elevation changes and coastal wind when choosing approach clubs. The club describes expansive greens and specifically promotes caddie help with lines and subtle breaks.
Prepare for the walk as part of the round. The club calls its hilly terrain a physical test and offers push/pull carts as well as advance-reserved caddies.
access: Public tee-time booking is offered directly by Chambers Bay. It is a walking-only course; arrange any accessibility needs with the club rather than presuming a standard riding cart will be available.
planning: Which standard or advance-reservation window applies to our visit, and what are its cancellation terms?
Should we reserve a caddie or use a pushcart, and can the club accommodate any mobility needs?
Which tees match our carries, and can we review the current yardage guide before arriving?

sources.title: Golf — course design, walking policy, booking and caddies

overview: Dubsdread is Cog Hill's No. 4, the Dick Wilson–Joe Lee championship course subsequently redesigned by Rees Jones. The club describes tight landing areas paired with large, undulating greens defended by heavy bunkering. That combination makes this a shot-placement round: reaching a fairway or green is only the first part of choosing a useful position.
playingNotes: Choose a tee using the full published tee table, not the course's Tour history. Cog Hill lists several options and a combination tee for No. 4.
Plan drives around the tight landing zones; an extra club off the tee is not automatically valuable if it brings the pinched area into play.
Heavily bunkered, undulating greens make approach location and recovery play central. Work on both sand shots and longer putts before taking on Dubsdread.
access: Cog Hill presents Dubsdread as a public-play course and invites bookings. Confirm No. 4 explicitly; Cog Hill's other numbered layouts are distinct courses, not substitute names for Dubsdread.
planning: Does our confirmation specify Course No. 4, and are there outing or maintenance restrictions that day?
Which published tee or combination tee fits our group without forcing repeated long carries?
Can we reserve rental clubs and our preferred walking or cart arrangement, and what warm-up facilities are available?

overview: The Severiano Ballesteros course is Crans-sur-Sierre's 18-hole European Masters venue in Crans-Montana, not its separate Jack Nicklaus nine-hole course. Geneva is a travel gateway, not the course's location. The club asks for precision and a complete game, and the tournament's 2026 update confirms further work to the seventh green and teeing area.
playingNotes: Use a current course guide rather than an old tournament map: the European Masters reported a complete renovation of the seventh green and an additional teeing option in 2026.
The club publishes a precision-focused 18-hole layout. Choose tees and approach targets from the current scorecard rather than inferring difficulty solely from professional tournament coverage.
Ask the professional how to account for the Alpine setting in your own club selection. No fixed altitude-distance adjustment is assumed here.
access: Visitor play is conditional on the club's published access rules, including recognised club affiliation and an exact-handicap certificate. Confirm eligibility and a Ballesteros reservation directly; a general resort visit or Nicklaus booking does not secure this course.
planning: Does our club affiliation and handicap documentation satisfy the current Ballesteros access conditions?
Is the full course available around tournament preparation, restoration and seasonal opening dates?
Should we stay in Crans-Montana for the tee time, and which onward connection from Sierre will accommodate our golf bags?

sources.title: Severiano Ballesteros Course — course and access conditions
2026 pre-tournament press conference — seventh-hole renovation

overview: The Majlis is Emirates Golf Club's original grass championship course and the Dubai Desert Classic layout, not the neighbouring Faldo Course. The official hole guide gives it more substance than a skyline backdrop: uphill approaches, blind second shots, water carries and sloping greens repeatedly influence club selection. Treat the tournament reputation as context for that design, not a promise of tournament setup.
playingNotes: The club's third-hole guide describes a blind second over a hill and recommends a sensible lay-up short of greenside sand for ordinary players rather than an automatic attempt in two.
At the fourth, water guards the right of the green; the club recommends using the left half and leaving an uphill putt where possible.
On the fifth, hugging the trees can shorten the hole but obstruct the approach. The official guide favours the right side even though it leaves a longer second shot.
access: Current Majlis visitor eligibility and available booking windows are unconfirmed in the reviewed course description. Obtain a course-specific confirmation from Dubai Golf; a Faldo booking or night-golf offer does not establish Majlis access.
planning: Can Dubai Golf confirm Majlis rather than Faldo, the current visitor requirements and our actual tee time?
Are there tournament-preparation or maintenance closures, and what is the cancellation policy?
Which tees fit our water carries and uphill approaches, and what rental and practice arrangements should we reserve?

overview: Fontana is an 18-hole championship course at Oberwaltersdorf, outside Vienna, with bunkers and prominent water hazards forming its main playing framework. Its official description emphasises a revised layout and changing pin positions, not merely its former European Tour role. The club says its bunker styling follows MacKenzie principles; that is not a claim that Alister MacKenzie designed Fontana.
playingNotes: Map the bunker and water positions from the current layout before selecting a tee. Fontana identifies both as recurring strategic challenges throughout the round.
Changing pin locations are part of the club's explanation of difficulty. Plan to the available section of green rather than assuming yesterday's target line still works.
The club offers both walking equipment and electric carts, as well as rental clubs. Choose the equipment arrangement with the golf office rather than arriving with an assumed cart allocation.
access: Current non-member eligibility and any handicap requirements are unconfirmed in the reviewed page. Fontana provides a start-time booking link, but the presence of that link alone does not establish unrestricted public access.
planning: Can non-members book on our dates, and what handicap or club-membership documentation is needed?
Which tees and updated course plan reflect the current layout and water carries?
Can we reserve rental clubs, a trolley or an electric cart, and are any holes or practice facilities under maintenance?

overview: Glen Abbey is Jack Nicklaus golf in Oakville, with a flatter outward section followed by a much more dramatic encounter with the Sixteen Mile Creek valley. The club welcomes public golfers as well as ClubLink members. Its Canadian Open history is meaningful, but the reason to study the layout is the change of terrain and the creek's effect on the inward holes.
playingNotes: The published course account distinguishes the flatter opening nine from the valley holes. Do not build the entire round's club-selection expectations from the first few holes.
At the eleventh, a steep drop to the fairway precedes an approach across Sixteen Mile Creek. Check both landing position and the approach carry from your tee.
The fourteenth doglegs right with the creek crossing the fairway diagonally and a demanding ledge in the green. Plan the crossing point and approach section rather than chasing distance alone.
access: The official ClubLink overview explicitly welcomes public golfers and ClubLink members. Availability still needs a direct tee-time confirmation; the clubhouse being open year-round does not establish year-round course operation.
planning: What public booking window applies to Glen Abbey, and are any outings or maintenance works restricting our date?
Which tees give our group sensible carries across the creek on the valley holes?
What walking or cart arrangements suit the descent into the valley, and are rental clubs and practice facilities available?

sources.title: Glen Abbey — routing and valley-hole descriptions

overview: Jack's Point follows the contours beneath The Remarkables beside Lake Wakatipu. John Darby's routing moves through tussock grassland, schist outcrops, bluffs and native bush, with fairways, greens and bunkers fitted to the terrain. The distinction is between playing through that landscape and simply looking at mountains from a conventional resort course.
playingNotes: Five teeing grounds on each hole provide different ways through the terrain. Select by carry and comfort rather than treating the longest tee as the standard visitor experience.
Use the course guide to distinguish playable fairway from tussock, rock and bluff edges before committing to a line; the natural hazards are part of the routing's identity.
The course's contour-led design makes the lie and approach angle worth assessing separately from the raw yardage. Do not apply an unsupported blanket mountain-distance adjustment.
access: The official site publishes visitor booking and seasonal operating information. A confirmed reservation is required, and scheduled winter maintenance and greens aerification can interrupt play; check the current notices rather than assuming summer or holiday dates are unaffected.
planning: Do our proposed dates avoid the published winter closure and December greens-aerification programme?
Which of the five tee positions suits our group, and is a current course guide available before play?
What are the current shared-cart, walking, rental-club and weather-cancellation arrangements for our reservation?

overview: Katameya Heights is a golf estate in Cairo's desert setting, with an Yves Bureau-designed championship course and a separate nine-hole course. The official facilities page identifies Bermuda tif-dwarf greens and tif-way tees, fairways and rough. Those are useful course-specific facts, but they are not evidence of a particular green speed, firmness or visitor entitlement on the day.
playingNotes: Specify the championship course when arranging the round; the separate nine-hole layout is not simply the back nine of the same booking.
Use the short-game practice greens for putting, chipping and sand play to assess the surfaces before starting. The club lists these separately from its double-ended range.

An official handicap index is required for all players according to the club. The facilities page supplies no basis for assuming an additional numeric handicap cut-off or unrestricted beginner access.
access: Current non-member and unaccompanied visitor access is unconfirmed. The club requires an official handicap index; contact its golf office to establish whether your group can play and on what terms, rather than presuming a resort tee sheet is public.
planning: Will the golf office accept our group as visitors, and what handicap documentation or member introduction is required?
Is our booking for the championship course or the separate nine-hole course?
Can we reserve the limited rental clubs or caddies, and when are the range and short-game areas available before our start?

sources.title: Golf Course & Academy Facilities — layouts, turf and playing requirements

overview: Keilir's Hvaleyri course at Hafnarfjörður is a round of two contrasting coastal settings. The club describes a front nine surrounded by lava and a back nine on a small peninsula. That is the course's defining golfing identity: the landscape around the opening holes differs from the more openly maritime inward half.
playingNotes: Study the front-nine landing areas against the lava setting before choosing an aggressive tee line; the official description does not establish that the lava areas are playable or carry-free.
Reassess wind and club selection when the round reaches the peninsula rather than carrying the same assumptions from the outward holes.
Obtain the current Hvaleyri scorecard and local rules to distinguish the actual playable boundaries from the dramatic surrounding landscape; this guide does not invent hole-by-hole carries.
access: Current visitor eligibility, booking windows and handicap conditions are unconfirmed in the reviewed official course description. Ask Keilir directly for a Hvaleyri tee time and its seasonal opening status.
planning: Is Hvaleyri fully open for visitors on our dates, and which booking and handicap rules apply?
Which tees suit our carries through the lava-front-nine and coastal-back-nine routing?
Are rental clubs, trolleys and late starts available, and what happens if wind or weather stops play?

overview: Kennemer is Harry Colt golf in the open dune landscape at Zandvoort, with 27 holes rather than one permanently fixed visitor eighteen. The club emphasises heavy rough and the prevailing south-westerly wind. The practical golf task is to confirm the day's loop combination and plan a controlled round through exposed fairways, not to assume every Kennemer booking follows the same sequence.
playingNotes: Ask which A, B and C loops make up your round and obtain the matching scorecard; a 27-hole club needs more layout precision than a generic 18-hole reservation.
Heavy rough makes the playable landing area more important than the broad dune view might suggest. Choose a line and club that leave a realistic next shot.
The club publishes winter-green placements for all three loops. Their existence does not mean they will be used on your date, so confirm the actual greens and local rules.
access: Conditional visitor access through the caddiemaster, not unrestricted public play. The official visitor page requires club membership and a qualifying handicap, excludes Sundays and reserves other periods for members; competitions and visitor caps can further limit availability. Confirm the current rules without relying on a numeric limit copied from an old listing.
planning: Will the caddiemaster approve our membership and handicap documentation for the requested day?
Which two loops are allocated, and will we use main greens or winter greens?
What member-reserved periods, competitions, weather restrictions and cancellation terms affect our tee time?

overview: Kytäjä's South East is Thomas McBroom's forest-to-lakeshore routing at Hyvinkää, not the club's separate North West course. The front nine moves through spacious woodland with elevation changes; the back nine opens along Lake Kytäjä. Wide fairways, deep bunkers and undulating greens give the layout its strategic scale without making every approach equally forgiving.
playingNotes: Prepare for two distinct halves: reassess shot shapes and club selection as the forested outward nine gives way to the lakeshore inward nine.
Wide fairways offer room to choose an approach position, but deep bunkers and contoured greens still require a target plan beyond merely finding short grass.
Use the grass range's bunkered target greens and the short-game areas to prepare for the course's sand and putting contours rather than limiting the warm-up to drivers.
access: Current South East visitor eligibility and booking or handicap requirements are unconfirmed in the reviewed course page. Confirm them with Kytäjä and specify South East; a North West booking is a different round.
planning: Can the club confirm South East, the applicable visitor requirements and its opening status?
Which tees suit our group, and what are the important carries between the forest and lakeshore sections?
Are the grass range and short-game areas operating, and do maintenance or competition dates affect the full routing?

overview: Marco Simone's Ryder Cup course is an undulating, predominantly open parkland layout near Rome, substantially renewed by Tom Fazio II and European Golf Design from the earlier Jim Fazio course. Specify the Ryder Cup course when planning this visit. The attraction is experiencing that reworked championship routing, not assuming televised match-play choices are sensible from a visitor's tee.
playingNotes: Elevation changes are part of the reviewed layout description. Assess the uphill or downhill approach independently of the printed yardage before choosing a club.
Use the current course map rather than an older pre-renovation guide: the official club confirms the routing was completely renewed for the 2023 Ryder Cup.
Choose your own tee and lay-up strategy instead of copying professionals' attacking lines. The reviewed sources establish the redesign and terrain, not a universal carry requirement for visitors.
access: A reviewed visitor directory lists advance-booked visitor play with restricted periods, but current eligibility, playing days and handicap conditions remain unconfirmed until the club approves the reservation. Ryder Cup history does not imply open daily public access.
planning: Is the booking for the Ryder Cup course, and which current visitor days and handicap documentation apply?
Are any holes or practice areas unavailable for competitions or maintenance?
Which tees are recommended for our group, and what walking, cart and rental-club arrangements can be confirmed in advance?

overview: Millbrook is a two-course golf destination in an alpine amphitheatre near Queenstown, not one anonymous resort eighteen. The Remarkables and Coronet courses use rugged terrain with tussocks, streams, schist stone, trees and even buildings in the golfing landscape. The resort calls the style alpine links; that description should not be confused with an assurance of firm seaside-links turf.
playingNotes: Confirm Remarkables or Coronet and get that layout's scorecard before choosing tees. A generic Millbrook booking does not tell you which eighteen you will play.
Use the current guide to locate streams, stone and other natural hazards before selecting a landing area; the resort specifically lists this variety as part of the design.
Five tee positions allow the same terrain to be approached differently. Select for the group's actual carries and approach clubs, not the resort's New Zealand Open billing.
access: Millbrook explicitly welcomes casual visitors as well as in-house guests and publishes arrangements for both championship courses. A hotel stay is not stated as a prerequisite, but the chosen course and tee time still require confirmation.
planning: Which course are we booking, and can we arrange both Remarkables and Coronet on separate days?
Will the New Zealand Open, preparations or maintenance change availability or the routing on our dates?
Which tees fit our group, and can we reserve club hire and a cart or confirm the walking arrangements?

overview: Montgomerie Maxx Royal is the Colin Montgomerie–European Golf Design course in Belek, built on sand among Mediterranean pines. The official description singles out its floodlit back nine. That makes the distinction between a full daytime round and a specifically arranged evening nine important; the lighting claim applies to this layout, not to every course in Belek.
playingNotes: The official sixth-hole guide highlights an undulating fairway and a long approach; assess the lie and remaining shot rather than planning solely from the card's total length.
At the fifteenth, the fairway narrows the farther the tee shot travels. Decide on a landing area before defaulting to driver on this short par four.
The back nine is the section identified as floodlit. Confirm whether the booking is a full daylight round or an arranged evening nine; do not infer eighteen holes under lights.
access: Current independent-visitor eligibility, hotel-package conditions and evening tee-time availability are unconfirmed in the reviewed course overview. Obtain written confirmation for the actual daytime or floodlit product you intend to play.
planning: Can golfers who are not staying at Maxx Royal reserve a round, and what visitor requirements apply?
Does our start permit a full daylight eighteen or a floodlit back nine, and what are the evening operating arrangements?
Which tees, rental clubs, cart arrangements and maintenance notices apply to the confirmed booking?

sources.title: Hole by Hole — official Montgomerie Maxx Royal playing guide

overview: Muirfield is an East Lothian links with an unusually legible structure: the outward nine circles clockwise around the property and the inward nine runs anti-clockwise inside it. Harry Colt's revised layout, later refined by Tom Simpson and Martin Hawtree, changes the wind angle repeatedly rather than simply sending golfers straight out and back along the coast.
playingNotes: Recalculate the wind on each change of direction. The club describes calm conditions as the exception and the two opposing circuits make a fixed wind adjustment unreliable.

Most landing areas are visible and relatively flat, and few bunkers are hidden according to the club. Use that visibility to pick a deliberate safe side rather than treating the links as a blind gamble.

The course page offers distinct medal and shorter blue-tee experiences. Ask which tees are allocated for your visit; a famous championship venue does not require every guest to play championship length.
access: Private club with conditional visitor play on designated Tuesdays and Thursdays. The published guidance requires a recognised handicap and restricts smaller-group bookings in peak months; those groups may need the cancellation waiting list. Confirm the current terms and acceptance before arranging the rest of the trip.
planning: Does our group size and handicap documentation meet the current visitor requirements for the requested day?
Is the reservation for a single round or the club's fuller visitor-day format, and what playing format and clubhouse dress rules apply?
Which tees, caddie arrangements and weather-related cancellation conditions will apply to us?

overview: New South Wales Golf Club occupies the rugged La Perouse cliffs overlooking Botany Bay. The club credits Alister MacKenzie's original routing and a recent Mackenzie & Ebert remastering. This is a coastal-terrain round rather than generic Sydney parkland, and establishing private-club access is an essential part of deciding whether it belongs in your itinerary.
playingNotes: Use an up-to-date guide following the club's recent remastering; an old routing account may not reflect the present hazards and playing options.
The official course description emphasises rugged terrain and a strategic routing. Assess the lie, contours and available approach before selecting a club solely from the yardage.
Check the day's coastal wind and the club's recommended tees before assigning aggressive lines. The reviewed overview does not justify invented hole numbers, carries or a promise of calm conditions.
access: Private club. Its official tour-operator page confirms limited unaccompanied weekday guest access, subject to special events, through approved providers. That is not a public tee sheet or a guaranteed weekend route; ask the club to confirm the eligibility and booking channel for your circumstances.
planning: Will the club accept our guest request, and should it come directly, through our home club or through an approved operator?
What current residence, handicap, playing-day and dress conditions apply to our group?
Is the full remastered course in play, and which tees and walking or cart arrangements are available?

sources.title: Tour Operators — limited private-club guest access

overview: Oitavos Dunes is Arthur Hills golf among Atlantic-facing sand dunes and umbrella pines at Cascais. The official account and reviewed course profile describe a mix of woodland and links-type holes, rather than an entirely treeless out-and-back links. The practical appeal is moving between those settings while adapting to the wind and choosing routes through the natural features.
playingNotes: Separate the pine-framed holes from the more open dune sections when planning the round; the landscape mix is a defining feature, not just scenery behind the fairways.
The operator explicitly highlights wind as part of the challenge. Recheck flight and club selection on exposed shots instead of assuming the conditions near the clubhouse apply everywhere.
Use the course's practice facilities to rehearse both a controlled flight and the normal approach game. The sources establish dunes and pines, not guaranteed running approaches or firm turf.
access: The operator invites golf visits and provides play enquiries, but the reviewed overview does not settle current non-member eligibility, handicap conditions or tee-time availability. Treat access as unconfirmed until Oitavos Dunes accepts your reservation.
planning: Can the course confirm our visitor eligibility and handicap requirements without a hotel package?
Which tees and current guide should we use for the dune and woodland sections?
Are there maintenance, competition or wind-related restrictions, and what are the cancellation and rental-equipment arrangements?

sources.title: Oitavos Dunes — Arthur Hills design, dunes, pines and visitor enquiries

overview: Portmarnock Golf Club occupies a narrow sandy peninsula north of Dublin, with 27 holes in shallow duneland. This is the historic club, not another Portmarnock-branded golf property. Its exposed setting and multi-loop identity matter as much as its Irish Open history: confirm the actual eighteen you are allocated before attaching a famous finishing sequence to your booking.
playingNotes: Ask which loops form your round and obtain the corresponding scorecard. The club's 27-hole inventory should not be presented as one automatic eighteen-hole route.
Prepare for a walking round. The official visitor information says visitor buggies are not available; arrange caddie or trolley details directly rather than presuming a riding-cart option.
Use the peninsula setting to prompt a wind check at each tee, not a promise of a particular breeze or firm surface. A coastal address alone cannot predict the day's playing conditions.
access: Conditional visitor play, not unrestricted daily access. The published 2027 visitor programme has a defined April–September season, designated playing windows and several members-only days. Confirm the rules for your travel year and an accepted time directly with Portmarnock Golf Club.
planning: Does our confirmation name Portmarnock Golf Club, and which loops will we play?
Which visitor dates and weekday windows apply in our travel year, and is the requested time actually accepted?
Can we reserve a caddie or trolley for this walking-only visitor round, and what handicap and dress documentation is needed?

overview: Praia d'El Rey is Cabell B. Robinson's 18-hole course near Óbidos, combining pine-forest parkland with Atlantic dunes and seaside links-style holes. Deep bunkers and sloping greens tie those contrasting sections together. Book the named Praia d'El Rey layout rather than assuming any golf offered through the resort is this particular course.
playingNotes: Plan for the change from pine-framed holes to the exposed dune and seaside sections; re-evaluate wind and target selection as the setting changes.
Deep bunkers and sloping greens make the landing section of an approach important. A shot that merely reaches the putting surface may leave a much harder next stroke.
The official site requires a valid handicap certificate. Use the current scorecard and club advice to choose tees rather than inferring visitor suitability from a resort package.
access: The resort offers course enquiries and publishes a handicap-certificate requirement. Confirm current visitor acceptance, the applicable handicap conditions and a Praia d'El Rey tee time directly; neither a hotel stay nor a general golf package is a confirmed start on this layout.
planning: Does the booking specify Praia d'El Rey, and what current handicap evidence must each player provide?
Which tees suit our group across both forest and seaside sections?
Are there maintenance closures, weather restrictions or event allocations, and can we confirm hire clubs and a trolley or cart before arrival?

overview: El Prat is Greg Norman golf across five nine-hole loops outside Barcelona. The club currently lists three full-length routings: Pink, Yellow and Green. They share parts of the complex but are not interchangeable scorecards; Green combines Abajo and Vallés holes. Decide which named course your reservation includes before applying hole-by-hole advice.
playingNotes: Confirm Pink, Yellow or Green and obtain that routing's current scorecard. The Green course uses a different combination of holes, so similarly numbered holes and playing notes cannot be transferred between routings.
The club's guide describes Pink's sixth as a par three with a large protective bunker and a raised, sloping green. If allocated Pink, assess the carry and safe putting section from your actual tee.

Yellow's sixth is described with a raised green protected by bunkers, while its closing hole is a long uphill par four. If allocated Yellow, save a realistic approach plan for the finish rather than borrowing Pink's hole advice.
access: The club-published visitor guide describes public visitor play subject to a federation card for the full-length courses. Confirm accepted documents, current visitor conditions and the exact Pink, Yellow or Green allocation with the golf office before booking.
planning: Which named course and nine-hole combination will we play, and can that allocation change before the day?
What federation card, club affiliation and handicap documentation will the golf office accept for each player?
Which tees and practice facilities are recommended, and will maintenance or competitions affect the agreed course?

overview: Royal Cape is a flat, tree-lined parkland test in Cape Town whose challenges come from narrow fairways, contoured greens, water and wind rather than hills. The club's detailed hole guide makes the south-easter a repeated strategic factor. This is traditional positional golf with a championship history, not a promise that a flat walk produces an easy score.
playingNotes: The opening hole usually plays into the south-easter; the club favours the right of the fairway when the flag is back left and warns against running the approach over the green.
The fourteenth combines a demanding drive with water in front and right of the green. Identify a realistic approach target and carry rather than attacking the flag regardless of wind.
On the fifteenth, water, bunkers and a strongly left-to-right sloping green complicate the crosswind tee shot. Use the actual wind and pin position to choose the target.
access: Current visitor booking eligibility and available playing windows are unconfirmed in the reviewed course guide. Contact Royal Cape directly for acceptance, any handicap conditions and a tee-time confirmation before arranging a golf day around it.
planning: Which visitor days and handicap requirements apply, and can the club confirm our actual tee time?
Which tees and safer approach targets are recommended if the south-easter is strong?
Are the full course, practice areas and preferred walking or cart options available, and what is the weather-cancellation policy?

overview: The Old Course at Royal Golf Marrakech is the Gustave Golias–Arnaud Massy layout identified by Morocco's golf federation, distinct from the later Menara course. The federation describes a club landscape of thousands of trees, making this a different Marrakech golf setting from the more open modern resort designs. Keep the Old Course identity explicit throughout the booking and course preparation.
playingNotes: Request the Old Course scorecard and starting tee. Menara's separate design credit and nine-hole specification should not be folded into an Old Course guide.
Use the heavily wooded club setting to prompt a positional tee-shot plan, but inspect the actual hole map before deciding that every fairway is narrow or every tree is in play.
The federation identifies the Old Course as a par-72 layout. Check the visitor tee and current routing rather than assuming that statistic describes a combined round with Menara.
access: Current visitor eligibility and playing conditions are unconfirmed in the reviewed federation profile. Contact Royal Golf Marrakech for an accepted Old Course booking and any handicap, caddie or accompaniment rules; the profile is evidence of the course identity, not an open tee sheet.
planning: Does the confirmation explicitly cover the Old Course rather than Menara or a mixed routing?
Which tees and current scorecard are in use, and what handicap or accompaniment conditions apply?
Are there tournament or maintenance restrictions, and can we confirm rental clubs, caddies and walking or cart options?

overview: The Serapong is Sentosa Golf Club's championship course beside Singapore's harbour, separate from The Tanjong. Its official hole guide shows how the lagoons, sea channels, sand and contoured greens shape the golf. The water is not just a skyline foreground: several driving and lay-up decisions require choosing how much of it to challenge.
playingNotes: The fourth sweeps left around a tidal lagoon. The club recommends the right-hand landing area for ordinary golfers rather than attempting the ambitious carry used by longer hitters.
At the sixth, the landing area sits beside a sea channel and the approach must negotiate sand and the rock formation called the Dragon's Tooth. Position the drive for a clear, controlled second shot.
The thirteenth narrows between water right and bunkers left. The official guide offers a fairway wood or long iron as the safer tee option, accepting a longer approach.
access: The official Serapong page publishes visitor categories and a direct booking enquiry contact. Current tee-time availability, handicap verification and guest conditions must still be confirmed with Sentosa; a Tanjong reservation is not a Serapong start.
planning: Can Sentosa confirm Serapong, the current visitor requirements and our accepted tee time?
Which tees fit our lagoon and channel carries, and what buggy or caddie arrangements are required?
What are the current lightning-suspension, rain, maintenance and cancellation procedures, including the effect on an unfinished round?

overview: Steenberg's Peter Matkovich & Hayes course uses the Constantia Valley's vineyards, pines and waterways as golfing features. Its character is especially clear in the official hole guide: strategic cross bunkers, an island-style seventh green, large putting contours and a closing hole divided by a meandering stream. This is a course to prepare for shot by shot, not simply a Cape Town estate backdrop.
playingNotes: At the fourth, cross bunkers create a genuine tee-shot choice: lay short for a longer approach or take them on for a shorter one. Decide the carry from your tee before reaching for driver.
The seventh green sits among sand and water. Treat finding the putting surface as the first objective rather than forcing a flag-hunting line.
The eighteenth's stream and repeatedly split fairway give the drive, second and approach separate decisions. Set a landing target for each instead of assuming one aggressive line will solve the hole.
access: Steenberg offers a visitor-booking channel and lists visitor practice and hire facilities. Confirm the current tee time and eligibility with the club; caddies and carts are described as arrangable subject to weather, not guaranteed inclusions.
planning: What visitor and handicap conditions apply, and is the confirmed time for the full Steenberg course?
Can we reserve a caddie, cart or rental clubs, and what weather restrictions could change those arrangements?
Which tees fit our cross-bunker and water carries, and can we use the chipping and putting areas before the round?

sources.title: Golf Course — design, hole-by-hole guide and visitor facilities

overview: Thai Country Club is Denis Griffiths's championship layout on Bangkok's outskirts, designed to adapt from everyday play to elite competition. The club describes a neo-classical design with a variety of holes and abundant water, and identifies the 1997 Asian Honda Classic as an early test of the course. Its tournament history does not replace the need to select a sensible visitor tee.
playingNotes: Map the water against the current tee-specific course guide before selecting driving and lay-up targets; the club explicitly describes water as a recurring feature.
The design is intended to accommodate both casual and championship play. Ask the golf office which tees fit your group instead of copying the professional setup.

Prepare for varied holes rather than assuming one standard line or club from every tee. The official overview establishes the design's variety, but it does not justify invented signature-hole carries.
access: The official club homepage publishes visitor categories, distinct from membership. Obtain direct acceptance and confirm the permitted day and start window; the current visitor table differentiates weekday and weekend/public-holiday arrangements, so do not assume identical access every day.
planning: Which visitor days and start windows are available, and what current handicap or introduction requirements apply?
Are caddies or carts required, and what is included or separately arranged in our confirmation?
Which tees fit our water carries, and what lightning, rain, competition or maintenance procedures could affect the round?

sources.title: Thai Country Club — visitor categories and booking information

overview: Royal Melbourne's West Course is Alister MacKenzie's routing over rolling Sandbelt land, with doglegs, bold bunkering and large contoured greens that reward the right angle of approach. It is not interchangeable with the East Course or a tournament Composite routing. The official hole guide makes the central idea explicit: a useful position often matters more than extra driving distance.
playingNotes: At the second, carrying more of the fairway bunkers can improve position, but the green slopes right to left and an overhit approach leaves a demanding return shot.
The sixth asks whether to carry the inside-corner bunkers or play left for safety; the longest drive is not automatically best if it leaves an awkward angle over the greenside bunker.
At the seventh, the protected right-hand part of the green offers a different putting task from the safer left side. Choose the target with the pin and your bunker tolerance in mind.
access: Private members' club. International and interstate visitors who belong to a golf club may enquire about Mondays, Tuesdays and Fridays, excluding public holidays and subject to availability. Reciprocal-club rights follow separate agreements. Obtain explicit West Course approval before committing to non-refundable travel.
planning: Will the club approve our affiliation and visitor request, and does the confirmation explicitly allocate West?
Which tees, caddie or walking arrangements and current guest dress rules apply?
Are tournaments or course works changing the routing or practice access, and what cancellation conditions attach to the visit?

overview: Torrey Pines South is the City of San Diego's municipal championship course on the coastal bluffs, distinct from the North Course. The city describes tight fairways, substantial rough, bunkering and length, with the South remodelled by Rees Jones. Its U.S. Open history sits alongside genuine public ownership; it does not mean the everyday tee or setup matches a championship broadcast.
playingNotes: Choose tees for your driving and approach distances before being drawn to the championship card. The city's own description identifies length as part of the challenge.
Tight fairways and rough place a premium on a playable tee-shot position; plan how to reach the next target rather than using driver automatically for the longest result.
Confirm that any course guide, scorecard or maintenance notice refers to South. North-course details and mixed-course tournament coverage should not be treated as interchangeable hole advice.
access: Municipal public golf, owned and maintained by San Diego. Confirm the applicable reservation procedure and resident or non-resident category directly with the city; public ownership does not guarantee a South tee time. Check the city's current arrival and check-in instructions.
planning: Does our reservation specify South, and which city booking category and identification rules apply?
What South-course maintenance and tournament restrictions affect our date, and what are the cancellation terms?
How early must we check in, and can rental clubs, practice access and our walking or cart arrangement be confirmed?

sources.title: About Torrey Pines — South Course, municipal ownership and playing policies

overview: TPC Scottsdale's Stadium Course is the Tom Weiskopf–Jay Morrish layout used by the WM Phoenix Open, not the separate Champions Course. Its best-known feature is the sixteenth, which becomes the tournament's Coliseum. The distinction between the permanent golf hole and its temporary spectator architecture matters when deciding what experience an ordinary visitor round will actually deliver.
playingNotes: The sixteenth is the Stadium's famous par three, but the grandstand-enclosed Coliseum is described as a tournament transformation. Do not expect the full arena on an arbitrary visitor date.

The short par-four seventeenth invites a decision between attacking and laying up. PGA Tour ShotLink notes record tee shots reaching both the green and the water; identify your safe landing area instead of copying the professionals' gamble.
Select visitor tees by your own carries and approach distances. The Tour association identifies the course, not the appropriate difficulty or tournament conditions for your group.
access: The official Stadium page invites golfers to book and play outside the tournament, with a direct tee-time link. Confirm the actual Stadium reservation and any current eligibility requirements; the separate Champions Course and WM Phoenix Open event access are different products.
planning: Can TPC confirm Stadium, our visitor eligibility and the accepted tee time?
Will WM Phoenix Open preparation, grandstand assembly or removal, or maintenance affect play and the sixteenth-hole setting?
Which tees suit our group, and what rental-club, cart, practice and cancellation conditions apply?

sources.title: WM Phoenix Open 2025 ShotLink notes — sixteenth and seventeenth holes

overview: TPC Summerlin is Bobby Weed's private desert layout, with Fuzzy Zoeller as consultant, routed through Las Vegas arroyos and canyons. Water features, mesquite and pines contrast with the natural washes rather than replacing them. Its PGA Tour pedigree does not make it a public Las Vegas tee-time option; access is the first question to resolve.
playingNotes: Use a current guide to distinguish the playable corridors from the arroyos, canyons and undisturbed desert washes that shape the route.
The official description includes numerous water features as well as desert terrain. Do not plan the round as a purely dry, bunker-only desert test.
Multiple tees on each hole are intended to accommodate differing abilities. Once access is approved, choose for your actual carries rather than the championship yardage.
access: Private membership club, not an open public visitor tee sheet. A member invitation or another club-approved access arrangement must be established directly; neither the TPC name nor a Las Vegas hotel booking guarantees a round at Summerlin.
planning: What member-hosted or other authorised access, if any, can the club approve for our group?
Does the accepted invitation cover our date and all players, and what guest conduct and handicap rules apply?
Which tees, cart or walking arrangements and practice facilities are available, and are there competition or maintenance restrictions?

sources.title: Golf at TPC Summerlin — layout, architect and natural features

overview: Walton Heath's Old Course is Herbert Fowler's open-heathland design in Surrey, separate from the New Course. The club emphasises length, smaller greens and the scope for traditional Scottish-style approaches, rather than a woodland target-golf formula. Phased winter restoration by Mackenzie & Ebert means the current course notice is as important to trip planning as the historic championship record.
playingNotes: Length paired with smaller greens makes approach planning central. Choose tees that leave manageable second shots rather than assuming the open landscape is forgiving.
The club specifically associates the Old with imaginative, traditional approaches. Check the day's surfaces before deciding whether a running shot or an aerial approach is appropriate.
Obtain the Old Course scorecard and current restoration notice. A New Course map or a generic 36-hole package does not establish the exact holes or conditions for this round.
access: Visitors are welcomed within published playing windows and subject to availability. The club's winter information limits longer multi-round plans because of daylight, while phased restoration can affect the experience. Confirm an Old Course time rather than treating general visitor access as a guarantee.
planning: Can the club confirm Old, the applicable visitor start window and any handicap documentation?
Will phased restoration, preferred lies or temporary restrictions change the course on our dates?
Is one round or a two-course day realistic within the current daylight and visitor windows, and can we reserve caddies or hire equipment?

overview: Wentworth's West is Harry Colt's Surrey championship course, distinct from the East and Edinburgh layouts. Its wooded, heathery setting and later alterations make it more than a generic London golf stop. The official club highlights moisture-control technology in the West greens, but that investment is not an independent guarantee of a particular speed or firmness for an invited guest's round.
playingNotes: The reviewed course account describes the second as a carry across a valley to a plateau green. Verify the current tee and carry with the course guide rather than adopting an old published yardage.
The seventeenth is described as a sweeping left-hand dogleg framed by tall trees. Position matters: a drive too far left can leave the next shot blocked even when it has travelled farther.
Ask about the current setup following the West's alterations. The club's SubAir system controls moisture; it does not justify promising tournament-speed greens or weather-proof golf.
access: Members and their guests, according to Wentworth's official golf page. This is not an established public-pay-and-play option. Secure a club-approved invitation that explicitly includes the West before planning travel or treating a tournament ticket as playing access.
planning: Has the club approved our member-hosted visit, and does it include the West rather than East or Edinburgh?
Which guest dress, handicap, arrival and host-accompaniment rules apply?
Will tournament preparation or course works affect the routing, and which tees, caddie and practice arrangements are confirmed?
